Question
========
The JSON standard defines a fixed set of value types that can appear in a JSON text. Which of the following is *not* one of them?

Answerlist
----------
* number
* date
* string
* object


Solution
========
According to the JSON standard, a value is always one of the following: an object, an array, a number, a string, or one of the three literal names `true`, `false` and `null`. There is no separate "date" type - dates are simply represented as strings, and it is up to the application reading the JSON text to interpret them accordingly.

Answerlist
----------
* False
* True
* False
* False
